{{Hatnote|This page is about the charity convention. For the 2001 Star Wars CCG World Championship, see [[2001 Decipher World Championship]].}}
[[File:FreedomCon 2001 banner.gif|thumb|right|260px|FreedomCon World Championships banner.]]
[[File:Virginia Beach oceanfront circa 2001.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Virginia Beach oceanfront hotels, circa 2001. Photo: Fredlyfish4.]]
'''FreedomCon''' was a charity gaming convention run by [[DeckTech]] on 15&ndash;18 November 2001 at the Sheraton Oceanfront Hotel in Virginia Beach, Virginia.<ref name="fc-home">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ FreedomCon home page], decktech.net (after the event). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011201221615/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ Internet Archive, 1 December 2001]</ref> DeckTech ran it after [[Decipher]] cancelled DecipherCon 2001, scheduled for the same dates and hotel.<ref name="tf-dcon">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/DecipherCon_2001_72163.asp DecipherCon 2001], TheForce.Net (15 June 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009001958/https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/DecipherCon_2001_72163.asp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="holland">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Special_message_from_Decipher_CEO_Warren_Holland_70685.asp Special message from Decipher CEO Warren Holland], TheForce.Net (3 October 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010073714/https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Special_message_from_Decipher_CEO_Warren_Holland_70685.asp Internet Archive]</ref> It ran World Championship events for Star Wars, Star Trek, Young Jedi and Jedi Knights.<ref name="fc-about">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/about.php About FreedomCon], decktech.net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020219012905/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/about.php Internet Archive, 19 February 2002]</ref> The Star Wars CCG event is the [[2001 Decipher World Championship]].

== 2001 Star Wars CCG World Championship ==

[[Bastian Winkelhaus]] defeated [[Martin Akesson]]. The top four were:<ref name="fc-home" />

# [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] (World Champion)
# [[Martin Akesson]]
# [[Hayes Hunter]]
# [[Brian Hunter]]

[[Scott Lingrell]] reached the final eight and posted [[Scott Lingrell FreedomCon 2001 - Final 8 Deck]].<ref name="fc-forum">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=75427 SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History], forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020; players' recollection of the 2001 top 8). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Recognition ==

[[Monica Jones]] wrote on 9 November 2001 that Decipher would not recognize FreedomCon as the World Championships.<ref name="fc-stmt">[http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Deciphers_Statement_About_Freedom_Con_70203.asp Decipher's Statement About Freedom Con], TheForce.Net (9 November 2001; statement by [[Monica Jones]], Decipher V.P. Marketing). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012022154/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Deciphers_Statement_About_Freedom_Con_70203.asp Internet Archive]</ref> The [[Players Committee]] lists Winkelhaus as the 2001 champion.<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org (World Champions list: "2001 - Bastian Winkelhaus def. Martin Akesson, held at FreedomCon - Virginia Beach, VA"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222454/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Internet Archive, 17 August 2023]</ref> The 2002 qualification system gave him a Day Two bye as FreedomCon champion.<ref name="hs">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/The_Hyperspace_Lane_to_the_World_Championships_68998.asp The Hyperspace Lane to the World Championships], TheForce.Net (9 February 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009001957/https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/The_Hyperspace_Lane_to_the_World_Championships_68998.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

== The event ==

Entry was $30 pre-registered or $35 at the door. 160 people attended. The championships raised $1,343 for the American Red Cross Disaster Relief Fund.<ref name="fc-home" /> Other winners were Brian Muller (Jedi Knights), Katie Billings (Young Jedi) and Ian Vincent (Star Trek).<ref name="fc-home" />

== FreedomCon Philadelphia (2002) ==

DeckTech held FreedomCon Philadelphia 2002 (FreedomCon II) on 4&ndash;6 October 2002 at NeoQuest Games in Lansdale, Pennsylvania.<ref name="fc-attend">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/attend.php Players Attending], decktech.net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030113235106/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/attend.php Internet Archive, 13 January 2003]</ref><ref name="fc2-home">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ FreedomCon Philadelphia 2002 home page], decktech.net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030112115941/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ Internet Archive, 12 January 2003]</ref> [[Michael Carr|"Mighty" Mike Carr]] organized it. The charity was the United Mitochondrial Disease Foundation.<ref name="fc2-home" />

The [[2002 World Championship]] was at [[DecipherCon 2002]], Chesapeake Conference Center, Virginia Beach, 1–3 November 2002.<ref name="dcon-fmt">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020810223927/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/events/worldsformats.html World Championship Event Formats & Prizes], decipher.com (Wayback, 10 August 2002)</ref><ref name="tfn-2002">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/World_Championship_Results_announced_64778.asp World Championship Results announced], TheForce.Net (3 November 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015165009/https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/World_Championship_Results_announced_64778.asp Internet Archive]</ref>
